Thomas King, PhD
attributes.description:
Dr. Tom King joined the Sabin Vaccine Institute in 2021 to oversee vaccine development initiatives for Ebola and Marburg. He also aims to add new products to Sabin’s vaccine pipeline to deliver affordable, accessible vaccines to under-served populations.

Tom comes to Sabin with a 25-year background in industrial biotechnology. He has served as the R&D director at private and publicly traded companies, including ImmunityBio and GlobeImmune. In these roles, Tom and his teams created animal models to study the immunogenicity of adenoviral, microbial and subunit vaccine platforms combined with protein-based immune modulation. These products, developed against eight distinct infectious disease and cancer targets, have led to 20 phase 1 and 2 FDA-regulated clinical trials. His work also required close collaboration with manufacturing, regulatory, and quality groups across public and private sector leaders — securing $250 million in funds and proceeds to further propel innovation.

Tom earned his PhD at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst. He is inventor/author of 46 patents and peer-reviewed publications. He is eager to strategically leverage his experience towards better health and quality of life for those in emerging economies by creating more efficacious vaccines that are affordable and accessible to all.

attributes.name: Denise Garrett, MD, MSc
attributes.description:
Dr. Denise Garrett is the Vice President of Applied Epidemiology at the Sabin Vaccine Institute, where she leads a team dedicated to generating epidemiological evidence for informed vaccine decision-making, optimizing vaccine use, and enhancing the impact of immunization.


Denise brings extensive expertise in epidemiological operational research, program leadership and management, infectious disease control and prevention, and vaccine effectiveness studies. Before joining Sabin, she served as a medical epidemiologist at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) for over 23 years. During her tenure, Denise focused on international health and research, overseeing numerous multicenter studies in both high- and low-resource settings.

Denise received her medical training, specializing in infectious diseases, and earned a master’s degree in human biology from Brazil’s Federal University of Minas Gerais. Additionally, she completed the Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) program at the CDC, where she received training in the practice of applied epidemiology.

attributes.name: Kiju deLeon, CPA
attributes.description:
Kiju deLeon leads all aspects of the Sabin Vaccine Institute’s accounting operations, including overseeing transactions related to general ledger, receivables, payables, payroll, budgeting and financial reporting. She works with the accounting team to ensure compliance with grant and contract requirements and with federal, state and local regulations.

Before joining Sabin in 2022, Kiju served in leadership roles in a variety of businesses, including a not-for-profit physician membership organization, a civil/structural engineering firm, and most recently, a large pension fund office. She specializes in process improvements and team building. She is also a member of the AICPA and the MACPA.

attributes.name: Amy Finan
attributes.description:
Amy Finan has led the non-profit Sabin Vaccine Institute as CEO since April 2016, expanding its vaccine research and development portfolio and global immunization programs. She has built key partnerships, broadened funding streams, and strengthened Sabin’s Board of Trustees and staff.

 

Since taking on the role, Amy has spearheaded Sabin’s pivot to an R&D strategy focused on developing  vaccines for disease threats with limited commercial appeal. In 2019, she led Sabin’s acquisition of a vaccine license from GSK and mobilized funding to advance Marburg and Sudan virus vaccines. These vaccine candidates have since progressed to Phase 2 trials, attracting more than $250 million in U.S. government funding.

 

Under Amy’s leadership, Sabin has delivered investigational vaccines during outbreaks and launched global health initiatives spanning surveillance, dosing strategies, vaccine access, acceptance, and uptake -- addressing diseases such as HPV, cholera, and malaria. She has also championed a deeper commitment to strengthening local partnerships in the countries Sabin serves while growing collaborations with government agencies and global health organizations, including the U.S. Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, WHO, Gavi, the Gates Foundation, CEPI, and Wellcome Trust.

 

After leading Sabin’s first organizational strategy rollout in 2017, Amy is now driving the launch of a new five-year strategy to further amplify Sabin’s impact.

 

Previously, Amy served as senior vice president at the Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO), where she expanded membership, revenue, and strategic initiatives. In parallel, she also served as president of the Biotechnology Institute, a BIO-founded organization dedicated to promoting life science education. Earlier in her career, Amy led corporate communications and investor relations at EntreMed and directed government relations at the National Association for Biomedical Research.

 

Amy studied at the London School of Economics & Political Science and earned a bachelor’s degree in political science from Trinity College in Washington, D.C. A native of Columbus, Ohio, Amy has lived in  the Washington, D.C., metropolitan area for more than 35 years.

About the Sabin Vaccine Institute 


The Sabin Vaccine Institute is a leading advocate for expanding vaccine access and uptake globally, advancing vaccine research and development, and amplifying vaccine knowledge and innovation. Unlocking the potential of vaccines through partnership, Sabin has built a robust ecosystem of funders, innovators, implementers, practitioners, policy makers and public stakeholders to advance its vision of a future free from preventable diseases. As a non-profit with three decades of experience, Sabin is committed to finding solutions that last and extending the full benefits of vaccines to all people, regardless of who they are or where they live. At Sabin, we believe in the power of vaccines to change the world. For more information, visit www.sabin.org and follow us on Twitter, @SabinVaccine.

attributes.name: Global HPV Consortium Description
attributes.description:
The Global HPV Consortium is a public-private movement to prevent Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) infection and eliminate cervical cancer as a public health concern. The Sabin Vaccine Institute, as the Consortium secretariat, along with a diverse set of partners, will mobilize a trans-disciplinary approach across the three pillars of Prevention (Vaccination), Screening, and Treatment. The Consortium will be guided by global goals, including the World Health Organization Immunization Agenda 2030 and Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative which :

 

• 90% of girls fully vaccinated with HPV vaccine by age 15 years

• 70% of women screened with a high-performance test by 35 years and 45 

   years of age

• 90% of women with precancer treated, and with invasive cancer managed

Sabin branded video backgrounds for Teams/Zoom/etc.


To change your background in MS Teams during a meeting, follow these steps:

  1. In the meeting window, tap More actions > Change background or Background effects .
  2. Select Add new and add the Sabin background from your device.
  3. After you make your choice, tap Done. If you don't see the Done button, tap the "X" at the top of the screen.

 

NOTE: if you have “video mirroring” turned on (which is the default), the Sabin logo will appear reversed in your preview screen. Rest assured, everyone else will see the logo in the correct orientation.

R&D Clinical Trials Final
attributes.description:
YouTube Name and Description:

Confronting Deadly Diseases: Sabin’s Vaccine Trials for Sudan Ebolavirus and Marburg

Vaccines are our best defense against disease. Yet, we still have lethal diseases that need a vaccine solution urgently. Sabin's R&D team is tackling two such threats: Sudan ebolavirus and Marburg virus disease. There are no approved vaccines for either of these viruses which have left behind a trail of outbreaks, ending many lives and livelihoods in Africa. Sabin’s vaccines are in Phase 2 clinical trials in Uganda and Kenya. Initial results are expected next year. Findings from Phase 1 trials and studies were promising, suggesting these vaccines are safe, fast-acting, and robust.

Nadia Afrin leads strategic communications, media relations, and stakeholder engagement at Sabin Vaccine Institute. She brings more than 20 years of experience in communications, advocacy, and knowledge management from her career with multilateral organizations and international NGOs.

Her work has  consistently focused on elevating complex technical topics through compelling storytelling that engages diverse stakeholders and supports policy change.


Nadia holds an MA degree in Science and Technology Policy from George Washington University and a BA in Economics and Astrophysics from Agnes Scott College.

attributes.description:
Jennifer Raymond is the vice president of CMC at the Sabin Vaccine Institute. In this role, she directs a team focused on ensuring that Sabin’s vaccines are developed, manufactured, and tested consistently, safely, and in compliance with regulatory standards. The CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) organization acts as the bridge between lab discovery and commercial production, handling formulation and process development, analytical method development and testing, and production.

 

Before joining Sabin in 2026, she worked in the pharmaceutical industry for more than 25 years, with a long focus on vaccines. She is a seasoned executive with experience leading technical operations, manufacturing, quality, and CMC organizations across the full product lifecycle — from early development through commercial launch. She has held senior leadership roles at both large pharmaceutical companies and innovative biotech firms, including GSK Vaccines, Novartis Vaccines, GreenLight Biosciences, and Icosavax, where she most recently served as Senior Vice President of Technical Operations. She brings deep expertise across multiple technology platforms and a collaborative, results-driven leadership style grounded in quality, compliance, and operational excellence.

 

Jennifer received her BSc in Chemical Engineering from the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, PA.
